interface.title: Epidemiological Cost Calculator (EPICC) v1.1.0 (ForeSITE)
interface.field: Public health economics / infectious disease epidemiology
interface.stage_of_work: Decision support and reporting: estimating outbreak response costs under scenarios before or during an outbreak
interface.what_it_is_for: Pick or load a declarative cost model, such as measles outbreak costs, set its cost and epidemiological parameters for your setting, run it across outbreak-size scenarios, then share or export the results as tables, Plotly charts, a link, parameter files or a report.

data.note: Bundled models: TB Isolation Cost Estimation, Measles Outbreak Cost Estimation and Measles Outbreak Costs in Oregon. The Measles one has 3 built-in presets (School or daycare, Healthcare facility exposure, Low-resource setting). The test file measles_model.yaml was also uploaded as a custom model; it gave the same totals as the bundled measles model. Only the measles model was explored, so the tasks below are measles-scoped.

tree.general: Estimate a disease's response or control costs under alternative scenarios and local assumptions, and share the result with stakeholders
tree.specific: Estimate measles outbreak costs (hospitalization, lost productivity, contact tracing) for 22/100/803-case scenarios with EPICC, and share them by URL, parameter files and a report (the TB Isolation and Oregon measles models were not explored)

features.name: Documented parameter form with provenance tooltips and change markers
features.general: A grouped form of numeric model inputs. Each input shows its description, unit and literature source on hover, steps with +/- buttons, and flags edited values so you can tell your changes from the defaults.
features.specific: Collapsible groups (Scenarios, Medical Costs, Lost Productivity, Contact Tracing) of number inputs with (?) help listing the description, unit and references. Edited fields and their groups get a [*] suffix, which turns on Save Changes as Preset and Reset to Preset.
steps: Hover (?) to read the description, unit and reference
See [*] on the field and its group
Reset to Preset to discard the edits
serves_tasks: Review each default assumption and its literature source
Undo manual edits back to the active preset

features.name: Layered preset stack
features.general: Apply several named bundles of input values on top of each other. The bundle at the top of the stack wins where they set the same input; reordering changes which values win, and a bundle can be removed.
features.specific: 'Add preset' combobox adds a preset to the Preset stack (an Upload box for XLSX/YAML preset files is also shown but was not tried). Each row has ↑, ↓ and ×. The stack is merged in reverse order, so the top preset's values win; the result is written to the parameter form and the URL.
steps: Pick a preset from Add preset
Add a second preset to the stack
Move a preset to the top with ↑/↓ so its values win
serves_tasks: Apply and combine named setting presets

features.name: Editable scenario list
features.general: Define the set of named cases a model is evaluated across. You can add, relabel or remove them, and every output gets one column or series per case.
features.specific: In the Scenarios group, each scenario has a Label and a Number of cases. Add Scenario / Remove Scenario change the list, and the table, bar, line chart and URL (scenarios=…&scen.custom_3.*) follow it.
steps: Type a label and number of cases
Run Simulation to get a new column and series
serves_tasks: Add another scenario to compare and re-run
Compute the cost breakdown across scenarios with the default values

features.name: Scenario cost report with interactive Plotly charts
features.general: After a run, a report shows a component-by-scenario cost table and linked charts: stacked bar, share donut and scaling line. You can hover, toggle series, zoom and reset.
features.specific: Results panel: table (Hospitalization / Lost productivity / Contact tracing / TOTAL by scenario, with CSV download, search and fullscreen), stacked bar 'Cost breakdown by outbreak size', donut 'Cost mix – large outbreak', line chart 'Cost scaling by outbreak size'. The Plotly modebar has PNG, zoom, pan and reset axes; legend clicks toggle series.
steps: Hover a bar segment for its value
Click a legend entry to hide a series
Drag a box to zoom, then Reset axes
serves_tasks: Compute the cost breakdown across scenarios with the default values

features.name: URL-encoded shareable state
features.general: Every input change is written into the address bar as readable query parameters, so opening the link restores the exact calculation.
features.specific: The address bar holds model=…, param.<id>=… for values that differ from the defaults, scenarios=… and scen.<id>.label/n_cases. Opening the link restores them, with [*] markers. Unsaved models edited in the Model Editor show a banner saying they can't be shared as a link.
steps: Open it in a new session
Run Simulation to reproduce the results
serves_tasks: Share a reproducible calculation as a link

features.name: Parameter export dialog (YAML / Excel)
features.general: Save the current inputs to a file in a chosen format so they can be reloaded later or shared.
features.specific: Save Changes as Preset opens 'Save Parameters' with a 'Select file format' dropdown (YAML or Excel). It downloads *_params.yaml, with each value commented with its description and range, or *_params.xlsx. Reloading such a file through the Presets Upload box was not tried.
serves_tasks: Save the current parameter set to a file

features.name: In-browser model editor with try-before-export
features.general: A tabbed form editor for a declarative model (metadata, inputs, formulas, cases, report layout, presets). You can test the draft in the calculator before exporting it as a file.
features.specific: Open Model Editor tabs: Metadata (title, description, authors), Parameters (id, type, label, context, unit, default, min, max), Equations (Python compute expressions), Scenarios, Report (markdown/table/graph blocks), Presets. 'Try in Calculator' runs the unsaved draft; 'Export as Model File' / Cancel; 'Load a different model file'.
steps: Pick a tab such as Equations and expand an item
Edit a field such as the Compute expression
Run Simulation to check the effect
serves_tasks: Modify a model's formulas and test the edit right away

features.name: Custom model loader (file / URL / code)
features.general: Bring in a model definition from a local file, a web address or a pasted code string. It joins the model picker for the session.
features.specific: The Other... dialog 'Load Custom Model' has tabs Upload File (YAML), Load from URL and Use a Model Code. Load adds '[Custom] <title>' to the Model combobox (?model=measles_model). Only Upload File was tried.
steps: Run Simulation on the custom model
serves_tasks: Load a model definition from a file

features.name: Report document export
features.general: Save the model's results report (text, cost table and charts as laid out by the model) as a document file to hand to stakeholders.
features.specific: After Run Simulation, 'Save report as DOCX' downloads <model>_report.docx (2,391 bytes for measles, contents unchecked); 'Save report as PDF' is also offered but produced no file in the headless browser. The report layout comes from the model's Report blocks (markdown, table, graph).
serves_tasks: Export the results as a report document
